column5: In src/lib/drive-client.ts:160–178 and 368–389, both name searches request only files(id,name,kind), perform one request, and immediately report absence when files is empty. Neither requests nor follows nextPageToken, so an empty intermediate Drive page can cause a false DriveNotFoundError or creation of a duplicate folder.

This duplicates C1: src/lib/drive-client.ts shows the same single-page searches in getAppDataFileByName and findFolderByName, with findOrCreateFolder creating a folder after a null result. It identifies no additional defect or distinct correction.

This duplicates C1's pagination defect in src/lib/drive-client.ts:160–178 and 368–389. The additional explanation of false not-found errors and duplicate folders describes the same consequences of failing to request and follow nextPageToken.

This duplicates C1's finding against the same getAppDataFileByName and findFolderByName implementations in src/lib/drive-client.ts. The cited revision and line ranges substantiate the same missing-pagination defect rather than a separate issue.

In src/lib/drive-errors.ts:59–80, the quota-reason allowlist contains only rateLimitExceeded, userRateLimitExceeded, and quotaExceeded. A 403 with dailyLimitExceeded and 'Daily Limit Exceeded' matches neither that list nor the 'rate limit' message fallback and therefore incorrectly returns DrivePermissionError.

This duplicates C5's incomplete quota-reason classification in src/lib/drive-errors.ts:59–80. storageQuotaExceeded is also absent and falls through to DrivePermissionError, but it is another instance of the same allowlist defect and belongs in the same correction.

This duplicates C5's dailyLimitExceeded misclassification in src/lib/drive-errors.ts:65–80. The existing quota branch already passes status to DriveQuotaExceededError, so preserving HTTP 403 adds no distinct defect.

This duplicates C5's incomplete quota-reason allowlist in src/lib/drive-errors.ts:59–80, including the additional omitted storageQuotaExceeded value described by C6. Both reasons require the same classification correction, not a separate finding.
